author: riskyvega
quote:
I waited 13 years for this, and somewhere along the way Rockstar forgot what GTA is supposed to be.

GTA is supposed to be a power fantasy. This is a chore simulator.

 I didn’t buy a Grand Theft Auto game to watch my fuel gauge, juggle a tiny weapon inventory, and sit through slow “everyday life” busywork between missions. Rockstar has dropped the “magic pockets” in favor of limited weapon slots, and the “realism” doesn’t stop there. Every system seems built to slow you down instead of letting you cause chaos. If I wanted to manage errands, I’d do my own. GTA used to be about freedom. Now it’s a to-do list with a Vice City skin.

The cut content is obvious. no first-person mode, no dual wielding, no prone stance, no infinite weapon wheel, no infinite fuel, and no easy way to recover a flipped vehicle, among others. Some of these things were in GTA 5 thirteen years ago. In before half of this is going to be locked behind DLC if ever released.

The main characters are exhausting. Jason and Lucia are supposed to be the heart of the story, but I couldn’t stand either of them. The dialogue tries way too hard to be edgy and emotional at once, and it lands on neither. GTA protagonists used to be fun to play as even when they were awful people. These two are just annoying, and you’re stuck with them for dozens of hours.

I don’t trust the 99. A score tied with Ocarina of Time for the highest Metascore ever recorded, and not a single mixed review? For a game that runs at 30fps on a PS5 Pro, cuts basic features, and costs more than ever? To me that doesn’t look like honest criticism. It looks like an industry too scared of losing access to the biggest publisher around to say anything bad. The critic score reads like marketing, not a review. Look at the user scores instead.

Overpriced, stripped down, and more interested in making you do chores than letting you have fun. 0/10.
